title: How Many CCTV Cameras Do You Need? Size Guide for Homes & Offices
excerpt: Simple formula to calculate the right number of cameras for your property. Includes placement guide for apartments, houses, shops, and offices in Delhi NCR.
author: Eye Smart Security Systems

faqs.q: What's the minimum number of cameras I need?
faqs.a: At minimum, we recommend 2 cameras: one at the main entrance and one covering the most valuable area. However, a single camera covers only ~60-80 sq meters effectively. Most properties need 4-6 cameras for comprehensive coverage.

faqs.q: Should I use one large camera or multiple smaller ones?
faqs.a: Multiple cameras with moderate zoom is better than one high-zoom camera. With multiple cameras, if one fails or gets blocked, you still have backup coverage. For a home, 2-4 cameras are usually optimal.

faqs.q: Can I install cameras myself to save costs?
faqs.a: You can install simple cameras, but professional installation ensures optimal angle, cable management, and system integration. Poor placement wastes the camera's potential. We recommend professional installation for best results.

faqs.q: How high should cameras be mounted?
faqs.a: Entrance cameras: 7-10 feet high. Perimeter cameras: 8-12 feet. This height captures faces clearly while being harder to tamper with. Too high misses facial details; too low gets easily damaged.

faqs.q: Do I need different camera types?
faqs.a: Yes. Use wide-angle (2.8-3.6mm) for hallways and corridors, standard (4-6mm) for main areas, and zoom cameras (6-8mm) for perimeter monitoring. We customize the mix based on your property layout.

content:
How Many CCTV Cameras Do You Need? Complete Guide

One of the most common questions we get from Noida, Ghaziabad, and Greater Noida customers is: "How many cameras should I install?" The answer isn't one-size-fits-all.

Too few cameras leave blind spots. Too many waste money on areas that need no coverage. This guide provides a simple formula to calculate your exact camera requirement based on property size and security needs.

The Basic Formula

Each camera covers approximately 60-80 square meters with clear facial recognition. For basic surveillance (motion detection), it's 100-120 square meters.

Formula: Property Size (sq.m) ÷ 80 = Minimum Cameras Needed

Examples:

  • 500 sq.m property: 500 ÷ 80 = 6.25, so 6-7 cameras minimum
  • 1000 sq.m office: 1000 ÷ 80 = 12.5, so 12-13 cameras
  • 200 sq.m apartment: 200 ÷ 80 = 2.5, so 2-3 cameras minimum

Camera Placement for Different Property Types

1-2 BHK Apartment (800-1200 sq.ft / 75-110 sq.m)

Recommended: 2 cameras

  • Camera 1: Main entrance/door (captures who's entering)
  • Camera 2: Living room or corridor (captures movement inside)

Optional 3rd Camera: Balcony or window (for high-rise apartments in unsafe areas)

Independent House (3000-4000 sq.ft / 280-370 sq.m)

Recommended: 4-6 cameras

  • Camera 1: Main gate entrance (wide-angle, 2.8mm lens)
  • Camera 2: Side gate/service entrance
  • Camera 3: Backyard/garden entrance
  • Camera 4: Main living area/hall
  • Cameras 5-6: Garage, valuable storage, or terrace (if needed)

Placement Strategy: Ensure overlapping coverage of all entry points. Leave no blind spots between the main entrance and back areas.

Retail Shop/Office (1000-1500 sq.ft / 90-140 sq.m)

Recommended: 4-5 cameras

  • Camera 1: Main entrance (captures everyone entering)
  • Camera 2: Counter/cashier area (high-definition, captures transactions)
  • Camera 3: Stockroom/back office
  • Camera 4: Interior aisle (wider angle)
  • Camera 5: Rear exit (if present)

Why this layout? Retail theft often happens at the counter. The entrance camera captures who enters; the counter camera captures what they do.

Large Office Space (3000-5000 sq.ft / 280-465 sq.m)

Recommended: 8-12 cameras

  • Main Entrance: 2 cameras (front and back of door, captures all entries/exits)
  • Corridors: 2-3 cameras (every 30-40 meters)
  • Conference Rooms: 1-2 cameras (optional, for sensitive businesses)
  • Parking: 2 cameras (if internal)
  • Server Room/Vault: 1 dedicated camera
  • Common Areas: 1-2 cameras (break room, stairs)

Industrial Facility/Warehouse (5000-10000 sq.ft / 465-930 sq.m)

Recommended: 12-20 cameras

  • Perimeter: 4-6 cameras (corners and gates)
  • Interior: 4-6 cameras (storage areas, production zone)
  • Loading/Unloading Area: 2-3 cameras
  • Parking: 2-3 cameras
  • Office Section: 2-3 cameras
  • High-Value Assets: Dedicated cameras on expensive equipment

Choosing Camera Lens Types (FOV)

Different lenses cover different areas. Choose wisely:

Lens (mm)Field of ViewBest ForDistance
2.8mm110°Wide areas, hallways10-15m
3.6mm90°Entrance doors, corridors15-20m
4mm75°Standard, versatile20-25m
6mm50°Focused monitoring25-35m
8mm35°Perimeter, zoom35-50m

Critical Placement Guidelines

Rule 1: Cover All Entry Points First

Main door, side gate, windows (ground floor), back entrance—every way someone can enter your property needs monitoring.

Rule 2: Ensure Facial Recognition

Cameras should be positioned at eye level for visitors (4-7 feet high). This captures facial details needed for identification. Too high = can't see faces. Too low = easily tampered with.

Rule 3: Overlapping Coverage

Cameras should overlap coverage by 20-30%. This eliminates blind spots between cameras and provides backup if one camera is damaged.

Rule 4: Protect Camera Placement

Cameras should be 8-10 feet high, angled downward 15-20 degrees. This prevents easy vandalism and captures faces better than front-facing angles.

Rule 5: Balance Wide & Focused Angles

Use one or two wide-angle cameras for overview. Use standard and zoom cameras for specific areas needing detail.

Budget vs Comprehensive Coverage

Minimum Budget Setup

  • Property Type: 2 BHK apartment, ₹20,000-25,000
  • Coverage: Entry + main area only
  • Trade-off: Some blind spots, but covers critical areas

Recommended Setup

  • Property Type: 3-4 BHK home, ₹35,000-50,000
  • Coverage: All entry points + main areas + garden
  • Benefit: Comprehensive, minimal blind spots

Premium Setup

  • Property Type: Large home/office, ₹60,000+
  • Coverage: Entire perimeter + interior + remote areas
  • Benefit: Complete coverage, redundancy, AI analytics

Special Considerations

Apartments in Secure Societies

If your society already has perimeter CCTV, focus on apartment-specific coverage: entrances, balcony, valuables.

Corner Plot Houses

These need more cameras—at least 6-8—due to longer perimeter and multiple potential entry points.

Row Houses/Villas

Similar to independent houses but often with high walls. You need cameras covering top of walls (12+ feet) and gates.

Shop + Residential Mix

Separate systems are better. Shop needs transaction-focused cameras; residential needs entry/interior monitoring.

When You Might Need Fewer Cameras

  • Small studio apartment: 1-2 cameras sufficient
  • Empty office/workspace: Basic motion-detection setup works
  • Gated communities with perimeter CCTV: Supplement with interior cameras only

When You Need More Cameras

  • High-crime area: Add extra coverage and zoom capability
  • Multiple valuable items: Dedicated cameras for each area
  • Customer-facing business: More cameras for transaction proof
  • Industrial facility: Camera per production zone + perimeter

Camera Placement Mistakes to Avoid

❌ Pointing at a Wall

Surprisingly common. Cameras installed but not angled properly, capturing useless footage.

❌ Too Much Sky/Roof

Should capture ground and lower areas where people move, not the ceiling.

❌ Backlit Positioning

Mounting cameras facing a bright window/sun creates silhouettes, making identification impossible.

❌ Blocked by Leaves/Branches

Trees and plants can obstruct views. Regular trimming needed, or relocate camera.

❌ No Audio Coordination

Cameras and microphones placed too close cause echo. Space them 10+ feet apart.

Modern Alternative: PTZ Cameras

Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras can cover larger areas with fewer units. One PTZ can replace 3-4 fixed cameras.

  • Benefit: Remote control, covers wider area
  • Cost: ₹15,000-35,000 per camera (2-3x standard)
  • Best For: Large properties, parking areas, perimeter

Conclusion

The right number of cameras depends on your property size, layout, and security priorities. Use the formula (Property Size ÷ 80), then adjust based on your specific entry points and high-risk areas.
